question: Can this study obtain adjudicated findings establishing that an alleged FCRA reinvestigation failure occurred?

board_finding.remediation: Require a judgment, consent order or examination finding before asserting the failure occurred.

conclusion: One source adopted (FJC Integrated Database); four rejected. The remediation was implemented as a control, and the control is now satisfiable with real data.

candidates.publisher: Federal Judicial Center, republished by the Free Law Project
candidates.admission_rule: Coded statutory basis: title=15 and section startswith 1681.
candidates.why: Codes disposition (how the case ended) and judgment (who it went for), so posture and direction are read from official codes rather than inferred from prose.
candidates.independence: NOT a new source family. Same federal courts as the RECAP connector; raises evidentiary standing only, never the independent family count.

probes.observed: 402 published opinions; respondents include Experian, Equifax, TransUnion
disposition empty on 8 of 8 sampled FCRA clusters; posture, procedural_history and syllabus also empty

blockers: Statutory admission cannot be verified locally: suitNature is empty on the free search endpoint and opinion snippets do not contain the statutory citation.
Disposition cannot be classified: posture, procedural_history and syllabus are empty strings on every row; the structured disposition field is on the 401 cluster record.
candidates.rejected_alternative: Inferring disposition from opinion prose. Rejected: this repository refuses keyword guessing where structured metadata exists, and misreading a motion-to-dismiss denial would convert an allegation into a finding.
candidates.rejection_reason: A token was obtained and the endpoints opened, but the outcome fields are unpopulated for modern federal opinions. Admission could not be verified locally either, since snippets omit the statutory citation.

probes.observed: 1248 documents; rules, proposed rules, regulatory agendas, Paperwork Reduction Act notices

candidates.rejection_reason: The Federal Register is a rulemaking gazette, not an adjudication register. The consent orders it carries are FTC proposed orders published for public comment ('Analysis of Proposed Consent Order To Aid Public Comment'), which are not final adjudications.

candidates.candidate: FTC Legal Library, cases and proceedings

probes.observed: Block page: 'The request resembles an abusive automated request.'

candidates.rejection_reason: The publisher explicitly refuses automated retrieval. No legitimate route is available to this study.
No machine-readable feed. Independently, CFPB enforcement shares a publisher with the CFPB complaint family already in the study, so its independence would need to be argued rather than assumed.

control_verification.check: Existing RECAP connector admission rule against live data
control_verification.observed: cause='15:1681 Fair Credit Reporting Act' on 12 of 12 sampled rows; cites_fcra admits 12/12

implemented_instead: core/adjudication.py: evidentiary standing (ALLEGED/ADJUDICATED) orthogonal to source family, with a deterministic posture and direction classifier defaulting to establishing nothing.
PG-09 and PG-13 changed from pinned FAIL constants to computed controls.
Finding.occurrence_established and StudyVerdict.occurrence_established_count report standing separately from independence.
connectors/fjc_idb.py: adjudicated outcomes with deterministic statutory admission and conservative posture classification.

live_run_finding.observed: First live cfpb,court,fjc run reported PG-09 and PG-13 as PASS.
live_run_finding.defect: IDB rows carry no narrative so all classified to the default mechanism, as did the complaints; corroboration matched them on both being unclassified.
live_run_finding.fix: The unclassified fallback is excluded from mechanism matching in both directions, mirroring PG-06's treatment of an unknown company.
live_run_finding.after_fix: PG-09 and PG-13 report WEAK: an adjudication establishing occurrence is present but does not corroborate a classified mechanism.

next_step: Mechanism-level corroboration is structurally unachieved from case-level metadata: neither the IDB nor docket metadata names the duty breached. Closing it requires document-level text from a joined docket, where RECAP coverage is uneven. Scope as research, not wiring.

docket_join.join_key: PACER docket number rebuilt from coded office and docket_number, plus district court id
docket_join.verified: 4 of 4 live IDB FCRA cases resolved to exactly one RECAP docket
docket_join.why_mandatory: An IDB row records that an FCRA violation was found but not which duty was breached (section=1681 on every record, subsection always empty). The docket's nature of suit is the only field separating a consumer credit claim from an enforcement action under the same statute.

case_that_made_it_mandatory.case: United States v. Vivint Smart Home
case_that_made_it_mandatory.problem: A genuine FCRA violation about improperly using consumer reports, not about reinvestigation. It was the study's only occurrence-establishing record.
case_that_made_it_mandatory.resolution: Excluded. An adjudicated record must be confirmed against a single consumer-credit docket before it can establish or contradict anything.

docket_join.effect_on_live_run: Occurrence-establishing records fell from 1 to 0; PG-09 moved from WEAK to FAIL.
